card.source: Cairns, Hass-Klau & Goodwin, 'Traffic Impact of Highway Capacity Reductions: Assessment of the Evidence' (Landor, 1998)
card.claim: When road capacity is removed, part of the traffic does not reappear elsewhere ('traffic evaporation'), but the share varies widely from case to case.

card.source: Evaluations of the 2016 closure of the Voie Georges-Pompidou (Paris right-bank lower quays)
card.claim: After the lower quays closed, monitoring reported traffic shifting onto nearby parallel routes, including the upper quays, alongside a debate about how much traffic evaporated.

card.source: Evaluations of London Low Traffic Neighbourhoods (e.g. Goodman et al., 2021)
card.claim: The effect of filtering streets on surrounding roads differs from site to site, so displacement onto other streets has to be checked locally rather than assumed away.
Residential streets have a limited 'environmental capacity': beyond a certain traffic level, living conditions degrade even if the street can physically carry more vehicles.

brief.target: Quai de l'Hôtel de Ville from Rue de Brosse to Pont Louis-Philippe

hypothesis.text: Closing the eastbound Quai de l'Hôtel de Ville reduces traffic on that segment by ≥70% (G1) under normal demand with no mitigation.
Displaced eastbound traffic shifts onto the top-ranked detour street Rue François Miron (living_street/residential), raising its flow by >30% and >100 veh/h (C1).
Displaced traffic also spills onto the second-ranked detour Rue de Brosse (living_street), triggering C1 there.
Network-wide delay rises by >10% and >20 veh·h (C2) because the parallel detour streets are residential/living streets with limited capacity (E4) and cannot absorb displaced flow without congestion.
A modal filter on the first-ranked detour (Rue François Miron, mitigation F1) eliminates the C1 spillover on that street without creating new C1/C2/C3 violations (verified).
A modal filter on the second-ranked detour (Rue de Brosse, mitigation F2) eliminates the C1 spillover on that street without creating new C1/C2/C3 violations (verified).

decision.rationale: Running the baseline closure under normal demand will reveal whether the policy achieves the ≥70% traffic reduction goal (G1) and whether it triggers a robust C1 spillover (>30% increase and >100 veh/h) on Rue François Miron, which determines if we proceed to mitigation or robustness testing.
